Subject: FinCraft — performance follow-up & TTFT ask (post-demo)

Hi Samir / Elena,

Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciate the candid discussion about your latency sensitivity and the browser/mobile streaming behavior. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on:

- Primary goals: minimize Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) for interactive flows, and keep streaming chunk cadence tight for the in-browser suggestion surface.
- Info we need from you: typical request QPS (sustained and burst), average request size (tokens), percent of requests from browser vs backend, and whether you prefer SSE vs WebSocket for streaming.
- Suggested initial SLOs to validate: p50 TTFT target, p95 TTFT target, acceptable chunk cadence (ms), and concurrency/throughput targets for a pilot.

Can you share:
1) a realistic traffic profile (sustained RPS and expected spike RPS),
2) three representative example payloads (short/medium/long), and
3) any hard constraints on p95 latency or retry windows.

Next steps:
- Once we have your profile, we’ll propose a pilot configuration (hosted or dedicated) and run a 2-week performance validation with concrete SLOs and telemetry.
- I’ll loop in Karthik for sizing and to document the pilot runbook.

I attached a short workbook with the fields we need — if you’d rather paste examples into a shared Drive link, that works too.

Thanks,

On Mon, Jan 12, 2026 at 5:10 PM Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Samir / Elena,
> 
> Thanks again for the demo time today — appreciate the candid discussion about your latency sensitivity and the browser/mobile streaming behavior. Quick recap and the asks we agreed on:
> 
> - Primary goals: minimize Time-to-First-Token (TTFT) for interactive flows, and keep streaming chunk cadence tight for the in-browser suggestion surface.

Thanks Jordan — useful summary. A few concrete numbers from our side to help you size the pilot:

- Traffic profile: sustained ~250 RPS during business hours, with predictable spikes to ~1,100 RPS for short reconciliation windows (1-3 minutes) and occasional daily bursts up to ~1,500 RPS for batch import periods.
- Payloads: average request is ~420 tokens after tokenization (short = 60 tokens, medium = 420 tokens, long = 1,200 tokens).
- Client mix: ~70% browser (desktop + mobile web), ~30% backend.
- Streaming preference: SSE (we prefer SSE because of proxy/edge compatibility and simpler reconnect semantics).
- TTFT targets we care about: p50 <= 120 ms for interactive flows; p95 ideally <= 350-400 ms — anything above that materially impacts UX.
- Chunk cadence: we’d like partials to arrive roughly every 100-250 ms for long responses so the UI can render progressive suggestions without jank.

Questions for you: how do you handle cold-start TTFT (warm caches vs cold model paths), can you provide an estimate for required capacity to hold 1,100 RPS sustained for a 3 minute window, and what telemetry will you provide to help us validate p95? Also please share an indicative cost for a 2-week pilot (hosted with reserved burst capacity or a dedicated pilot).

I’ll attach three sanitized examples (short/medium/long) to this thread by EOB.

—Samir

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <s.patel@fincraft.ai>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@fincraft.ai>

Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinCraft — performance follow-up & TTFT ask (post-demo)

Thanks Samir — that profile is perfect and very actionable. Looping Karthik in now to confirm sizing, but a quick read from the platform side:

Proposed pilot (initial):
- Duration: 2 weeks of validation with telemetry capture.
- Mode: Hosted with reserved burst capacity; option to move to a short dedicated pool for the busiest windows if we see sustained bursts above our reserved envelope.
- SLOs to validate in pilot: p50 TTFT <= 100 ms; p95 TTFT <= 400 ms for interactive flows (browser clients). Note: p50 goal is aggressive but doable with prefix caching and warm KV-cache; p95 allows headroom for occasional backend fan-in.
- Concurrency/throughput targets for pilot: sustain 300 RPS, support controlled bursts to 1,200 RPS for 1-3 minute windows. We’ll instrument to measure per-route concurrency and offload large long-poll requests to a separate pool if needed.
- Streaming transport & cadence: we recommend SSE for your use case. Chunk cadence target: 100-250 ms per chunk for long responses; we’ll tune token emission size to balance tokenization overhead and perceived latency.

Attachments I’m adding to the thread: fincraft-ttft-profile.csv (your template with sample rows populated) and speedfront-streaming-requirements.pdf (short doc with the pilot measurement plan and telemetry fields).

Open items for you before we kick off the pilot:
1) Confirm which mode you prefer for the pilot (hosted reserved vs short dedicated trial).
2) Share the three sample payloads (or link to the Drive folder).
3) Confirm any strict p95 ceilings that would force an immediate escalation (e.g., regulatory SLA).

Telemetry we’ll provide during the pilot: per-request TTFT (p50/p90/p95/p99), chunk emission cadence histograms, KV-cache hit rates, per-model concurrency, and token-level cost breakdown.

If that looks good I’ll draft a short pilot runbook and pilot config and Ben/Karthik will validate capacity. Proposed next call: Monday 19 Jan 10:00am PT to review the runbook and align on ramp cadence.

Thanks — looping in Ben and Karthik to action sizing and runbook.

Jordan / Ben,

Got it — I’ll run a quick capacity check against the 1,200 RPS burst with the request-size distribution Samir provided and propose a pilot config by EOD Friday. Initial notes:

- With prefix/KV warm cache we can generally get p50 TTFT ~70-110 ms for the token sizes Samir called out; p95 depends on cold-start frequency and queueing during bursts.
- I’ll include two pilot modes in the runbook: (A) Hosted reserved with autoscaled burst policy (cost-efficient, quick turn-up) and (B) short dedicated pool for the 2-week window if FinCraft wants isolation for noise-sensitive flows.

I’ll attach a sizing spreadsheet and a sample pilot config to the runbook. I’ll also add a link to the observability dashboard and the initial trace spans we want to capture.

Karthik
